article: We assume that recommender systems are more successful, when they are based on a thorough understanding of how people process information. In the current paper we test this assumption in the context of music recommendations. We gather data about music preferences and listening habits of a group of participants and then analyze the data to identify patterns and preferences. We use this information to develop a music recommendation system that tailors recommendations to the individual preferences of each user. To assess the success of our system, we conduct a user study in which participants are asked to listen to samples of recommended music and rate their enjoyment. We compare the ratings of our personalized recommendations to those of a baseline recommendation system that does not take into account individual preferences. Our results show that our personalized recommendation system outperformed the baseline system, indicating that a thorough understanding of user preferences and habits can lead to more successful recommendations. This supports the notion that recommender systems should be developed with a focus on user behavior and preferences. Overall, our research highlights the importance of taking a user-centered approach in the development of recommender systems, particularly in the context of music recommendations.

article: They have always been our protectors. During the day we did not know where they went when turned to stone, perhaps to the Ether to regain their power, perhaps to fight in the Abyss to protect the souls of those departed. At night was a different story, they would come here..... and they would come alive. I was but a boy of nine summers when I first saw them come to fight the "Wrongs," spirits given form by darkness to torment and kill. My village had always been peaceful, we only had pitchforks and a few rusty swords from wars fought long ago. The sounds the Wrongs made on the wind would chill the bones of even the strongest person, and as children we were frightened. The Wrongs descended upon our village howling and screaming in torment and agony. We gathered in the small chapel with the head priest of the Veiled Divine blessing the door, hoping desperately they would not enter. That was all we had at the time..... hope..... hope and prayer. As the Wrongs got closer we could hear them slaughter the livestock, smash doors, and trying to find any living soul to devour. At first we thought it was the end, especially when we heard the wings over top our small building..... but then..... the screams outside turned to fear, and we heard the growls and vicious language of something else entirely. Peeking outside the window, I saw great hulking stone creatures with demonic faces actually fighting these shadow wrapped beings! I had never seen a Wrong before, nor a gargoyle, but the stoney creatures fought tooth and claw. The battle was over quickly, with the stone statues being victorious, driving the Wrongs back from our village. Then without a second thought or explanation the gargoyles took off back into the night sky, disappearing. We were alive, our village was spared, and we could rebuild the damage. Many of us that night took to doing the only sensible thing we could think of..... carving a gargoyle for our own village. There are nights when I wake to look outside and find our stone guardian missing, but I have never heard the sounds of the Wrongs come close to our village since. Couldn't keep it contained to 2, deal with it.

article: The primary obstacle to developing technologies for low-resource languages is the lack of usable data. In this paper, we report the adoption and deployment of 4 technology-driven methods of data collection for low-resource languages: crowd-sourcing, machine translation, automated web-crawling, and data sharing. These methods have been used to gather and process data for languages such as Amharic, Hausa, Swahili, and Yoruba. Crowd-sourcing involves enlisting the help of a large group of people, often via the internet, to contribute data or complete tasks such as speech or text annotation. This method can be highly effective for low-resource languages that lack the resources to hire a large team of linguists or language experts. Machine translation involves using algorithms to automatically translate text from one language to another. While not always perfect, machine translation can be a useful tool to help collect data in low-resource languages. It can also help to bridge the gap between different languages, making it easier for speakers of different languages to communicate with each other. Automated web-crawling involves using software to automatically search the internet for relevant data. This method can be highly effective for low-resource languages that lack a sufficient amount of data available online. Finally, data sharing involves collaborating with other organizations or individuals to share data and resources for the benefit of language development. This can include sharing data sets, software tools, and linguistic knowledge. By adopting and deploying these technology-driven methods of data collection, it is possible to overcome the primary obstacle to developing technologies for low-resource languages. With more data available, it becomes easier to develop tools such as speech recognition, machine translation, and language learning resources. This in turn can help to promote the use and preservation of endangered languages, and provide greater access to information and opportunities for speakers of low-resource languages.

article: TL;DR: I believe that burning a book can be a symbol of disagreement with the ideas presented within that book, that it does not necessarily mean that you cannot handle the opposing opinions presented in that books, and that it is never destroying information. I'm shocked to find that so many people, even people whom I agree with on several other topics, believe burning a book is an inherently immoral thing to do. When asked why, they say "Burning a book is destroying knowledge, and only those who hate knowledge would do so." However, I believe it is a symbol of disagreement. Firstly, if it's a book which has thousands or millions of copies in print, then burning one copy is not destroying knowledge, since other copies exist and are easily accessible. Secondly, I don't believe every book represents knowledge. A book like Mein Kampf is inherently different from a book like On the Origin of Species, because Mein Kampf contains the opinions and philosophy of the author, but On the Origin of Species contains factual information (I'm using Mein Kampf in this example, because it's the closest thing to a universally hated book that I can think of). If we believe that every book represents knowledge, then we must also believe that every author is also knowledgeable, or wise, which brings up a problem when different books contradict each other. That is a generalization, and it limits our understanding of the topics the book is about. Instead, I think we should judge each book by its content, and, by extension, the knowledge or wisdom of its author. So, Mein Kampf doesn't represent knowledge simply because it is a book. Now, say I finish reading Mein Kampf, and I am disgusted and reviled by it, so I choose to show my disagreement and disgust by burning it. We have already established that I'm not destroying knowledge, because there are other copies, and the book does not represent knowledge just because it is a book (it only represents knowledge or wisdom if we subjectively decide its author or opinions are wise, or if it contains facts). How, then, is burning it immoral? What other reasons are there that burning it is a bad thing to do? Change my view. Hello, users of CMV! This is a footnote from your moderators. article: Grandpa Earl looked his grandchild in the eyes and smiled the kindly smile that Connor loved so much. His smile was a reflection of his kind soul. Earl always had a smile or a joke at the ready whenever someone needed it. Sometimes even when they didn't know they did. Earl knew his grandson needed a smile now. "Does it hurt, Grandpa?" Connor asked. "The cancer?" Earl, honest to a fault, said, "Yes. Yes it does, son." "I don't want you to go, but I don't want you to hurt anymore." Connor swiped at his eyes with his shirtsleeve and tried to put on a brave face for this man who raised him after his mother had died just three years earlier. "Remember when I fell and hurt my teeth? You came out and took me to the doctor. Does it hurt like that?" "No, Connor, not like that. It's more like..." Earl winced and continued, "more like just really sleepy, but you can't just tap a nap and feel better." Connor tried stop the tears but couldn't. His grandfather had been a large, strong man for as long as he could remember but over the last few months had atrophied to nothing. His sallow skin stretched taut across his knuckles, knees, and shoulders. Every time Connor looked at him he was reminded of how quickly he had withered away. Earl noticed the way Connor looked at him, and it saddened him, too, but he smiled. It seemed to be the only thing about him that never withered. "Connor, hand me my wallet. It's on the nightstand." Connor followed the trembling hand as it pointed and he tried to ignore the tubes going into the machines, into his grandpa. He picked up the worn leather wallet and placed it in Earl's hand. "Son, I have always kept this in my wallet and whenever I've had a tough day I think about it. My grandfather told me about this when he died, and he said his grandfather did the same. It's a tradition in our family. And now A coughing fit racked Earl's frail form. Connor watched, wishing he could help. "Now, I'd like to show it to you. Keep it for your grandson, but I don't want you to forget about it. I'd like you to keep this in your wallet for those gloomy days." "I don't have a wallet." "You don't? Well, then, we'll have to fix that." Earl emptied the contents of his wallet onto the bed next to him. He held out the wallet to Connor who took it reverently. "Promise me you won't forget, Connor." "I won't forget. I promise." Tears spilled freely down Connor's face. "Look in the billfold pocket." Grandpa Earl smiled in contentment and closed his eyes. Connor opened the wallet, the softened leather creaking but inaudible over the sound of the machines surrounding his grandfather. He looked into the wallet and saw a folded piece of paper in the corner. He took it out and turned it over in his hands. Connor glanced up at his grandfather, who had stopped breathing. Knowing that his grandfather had died, but wanting to honor his last moment before interrupting it with the hospice nurse and the calls he knew he'd have to make Connor stood and kissed his grandfather on his still-warm forehead. He looked down at the piece of paper and opened it. A naked picture of his grandmother stared back at him.

article: This will probably get buried as I'm late to the party, but couldn't resist - the prompt is too good! This isn't that horrifying either, I just came up with it in traffic and kind of went with it. Good practice I guess. Bank station. The busiest on the network, nearly a hundred thousand passengers each morning travel through here, arriving to make their daily trudge through the city of London to their jobs. Most of them work in banking. They're easy to spot, with suits from Saville Row, shirts from Jermyn Street, and morals darker than the deepest recesses of Soho. Profiling a target is a doddle, and the execution comes naturally. Growing up on the estate, I was never going to be allowed into the rarefied air of the Bank of England or Lloyds of London. Once Mum had her benefits cut, I had to pay my way, it's not uncommon. Lads on BMX bikes move weed and whatever else they can get their hands on, but I was never tough enough to look after myself in those gangs. I ended up shoplifting, a quick stroll over to Oxford Circus, snip off the tags and tailgate a tourist out. Easy. Too easy. There's no skill to shoplifting, not like pickpocketing. I had a good teacher, a modern day Fagin if you will, though the flat caps of Oliver Twist were replaced by snapbacks, tags still attached of course. After a few years I went solo, still staying in touch with my old mates to make I wasn't stepping on anyone's toes. You rarely get a nicely worded letter from these boys if you're on their patch. Bank is so busy I can act with impunity, plenty of bankers for everyone. This one was perfect. I saw him run through the barriers, flustered, late, fumbling with his oyster card. He carefully checked his wallet before throwing the card in there, a flash of blue still visible as he slid it into his inside jacket pocket. This was almost too easy. I moved towards the door where he was stood, ostensibly to pick up a discarded copy of the Metro from a seatback. I didn't feel like reading, but it looks natural, and a freesheet is a bloody good prop, even if it is plastered in the latest story of debauched footballers. He was lost in his own world, checking his phone every five seconds, looking for the red blinking LED that has enslaved so many in this city. Even easier. He goes for the door, I watch his shoulders, tailing him through the barriers as he taps the wallet on the reader. He's going left, towards the exit for the Bank. I feint left and go right, my shoulder crashing into his chest. A flutter of newsprint and a thousand tuts from the commuters and I'm home and dry, the soft leather wallet nestling in my jacket now. I cross the platforms and jump on a tube heading east, time for a spot of lunch and a bit more work. Westfield Stratford, a hell of a shopping centre, and close enough to home to know shorten my commute back. I'm in need of a new t-shirt and I guess old habits die hard. Maybe a quick lift to top up the beer kitty for tonight. Quick scan and boom. A yank, can spot them from a mile off. They always dress like they're going into battle, rucksacks, sunnies, hat, bottles of water, as if anywhere outside of the USofA lacks even basic amenities. Not that I'm complaining, all those pockets make theft a doddle. I stroll past to get a look at the bag, but before I can she turns, and I freeze. "Hey, can you help me?" I was right, definitely American. Right, new tack. The accent goes on, no more wide boy charm, time for the full Cumberbatch.'I certainly hope so my dear, how can I be of service to you?' She smiles sweetly, and asks for some advice. Don't hang around with reprobates like me would be a good start, luv. Keep it moving "Let's walk and talk, it's a big place and we won't see it all from standing still." I introduce her to a few shops, she's in London for 2 days before her friends fly in. "Well it's a terrible shame for a lovely lady like you to be all alone. I wouldn't be much of a gentleman if I didn't offer to keep you company for a while. Fancy a spot of lunch?" She's in. Wahaca. Chelada. Tostada. We chat, it beats eating lunch alone. She's tidy, decent chassis on her in a pair of shorts and a hollister tee. Long blonde hair and a tendency to use'like' as punctuation, I'd guessed she was from California long before she divulged that fact. Whether it was the light glinting off her straw coloured locks, or the refraction of it through the amber beer, I felt good. I pay for lunch and take my leave, demanding only a hug as payment for her company. As we embrace I slide fifty quid out of her unguarded pocket, which covers lunch and my time. Off home, stopping on the way to pick up a henry and some king size rizla for the evening ahead. Through the door, trainers off and jacket over the chair, time for a brew. Fucking hell, I almost forgot, that wallet I took this morning. Chatting to that American bird distracted me more than I thought. Good job I wrote my number on the back of a tube ticket for her. I try not to bring evidence home if I can help it. Wallets get stripped of the good stuff and binned, phones are fenced down the local before I get home, the more unusual stuff I take a view on. Let's take a look at the wallet. It's nicer than I thought. Hand stitched, the leather is softer than I've ever felt before. The tip of the oyster card still peeks out from it. Two hundred bats cash. Nice. American Express Platinum, standard, and a nice way to assuage my guilt. Anyone with one of these can afford to lose a few bob. Few more bits and bobs. Mostly crap. Still, no stone unturned and all that. There's a slip of paper tucked inside, folded carefully. It's a photo. Who even carries photos any more? A photo of a baby in an incubator. Shit. That's what he was looking at. On the phone. He wasn't waiting for notification, he was looking at the wallpaper, the very same photo. Fuck it, he's got a digital copy of it then, nothing fifty pence at Boots can't solve for a reprint. There's more paper on the other side of the pocket, but it doesn't look like cash, I take a quick look so I can bin what I don't need on the way to the pub. Order of Service. Oh Christ. She was called Molly. He buried her yesterday. Poor Bastard. His driving licence is still in the wallet. I have to send this back. It's not fair. This is never what I set out to do. The address goes on the envelope, I'll throw it in the post box tomorrow somewhere in the city. Not popping evidence in the box at the bottom of the tower. For now, let's work on this henry. - I'm at Oxford Circus today, I don't want to go back to Bank in case I see him again. I'm not afraid, just ashamed. The letter goes in the postbox, swallowing at least some of my guilt in its wide red mouth as well. Time to go to work. Same routine, I take a seat and wait for some idiot tourist to advertise themselves. Another yank dressed like they're off to battle Rommel jumps on, and I grab my prop. No footballer today though. Seems some banker decided to take the quickest route from the top of the walkie talkie to the slabs below. I've seen that name before. Not half an hour ago as I dropped it through the slot.

article: The flexibility of the inference process in Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) has recently led to revising traditional probabilistic topic models giving rise to Neural Topic Models (NTM). Although these approaches have significant differences, they share the common goal of learning the latent structure of a dataset in an unsupervised manner. VAEs and NTMs are particularly useful for text data, where the goal is to discover the underlying topics that are present in the corpus. In a VAE, the model is trained to reconstruct the input data and generate new samples by learning a compressed representation of the data in a lower-dimensional latent space. The approach is unsupervised, meaning that the model does not have access to any labels. In contrast, an NTM takes a similar approach but uses a neural network to represent the topic model. The model learns to represent the topics as a distribution of words, and the generative process is conditioned on both the topic and a document-specific distribution. Overall, these models provide a powerful framework for discovering the latent structure of text data, allowing for improved modeling and analysis of complex, high-dimensional datasets.

article: Creating fake images and videos such as "Deepfake" has become much easier these days due to the advancement in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Moreover, recent research such as the few-shot learning can create highly realistic personalized fake images with only a few images. Therefore, the threat of Deepfake to be used for a variety of malicious intents such as propagating fake images and videos becomes prevalent. And detecting these machine-generated fake images has been more challenging than ever. In this work, we propose a light-weight robust fine-tuning neural network-based classifier architecture called Fake Detection Fine-tuning Network (FDFtNet), which is capable of detecting many of the new fake face image generation models, and can be easily combined with existing image classification networks and fine-tuned on a few datasets. In contrast to many existing methods, our approach aims to reuse popular pre-trained models with only a few images for fine-tuning to effectively detect fake images. The core of our approach is to introduce an image-based self-attention module called Fine-Tune Transformer that uses only the attention module and the down-sampling layer. This module is added to the pre-trained model and fine-tuned on a few data to search for new sets of feature space to detect fake images. We experiment with our FDFtNet on the GANs-based dataset (Progressive Growing GAN) and Deepfake-based dataset (Deepfake and Face2Face) with a small input image resolution of 64 64 that complicates detection. Our FDFtNet achieves an overall accuracy of 90.29 in detecting fake images generated from the GANs-based dataset, outperforming the state-of-the-art.

article: This paper introduces the variational Renyi bound (VR) that extends traditional variational inference to Renyi's a -divergences. This new family of variational methods unifies a number of existing approaches, and also offers new possibilities for model selection and posterior approximation. The VR bound modifies the standard evidence lower bound (ELBO) objective, by replacing the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence term with a Renyi divergence. Renyi divergences are a more general class of divergences that include the KL divergence as a special case. The VR bound can be used to approximate any posterior distribution that can be expressed as an exponential family distribution, and it can handle complex models with non-conjugate priors. The VR bound also allows for the exploration of the entire space of Renyi divergences, which can be used for both model selection and sensitivity analysis. Overall, the VR bound opens up new possibilities for flexible and effective variational inference, and can be applied in a wide variety of applications in machine learning, statistics, and beyond.

article: It is a challenge to specify unambiguous distance (UD) in a phase-based ranging system with hopping frequencies (PRSHF). In this letter, we propose to characterize the UD in a PRSHF system by analyzing the frequency response of the received signal. Specifically, we utilize the frequency-domain characteristics of the signal in each frequency hop to extract phase information that can be used to estimate the distance between the transmitter and receiver. To achieve this, we first analyze the frequency response of the transmitted signal across all frequency hops. We then use this information to generate a reference signal with known phase information. Next, we compare the received signal with the reference signal to determine the phase difference between them. Finally, we use this phase difference to estimate the distance between the transmitter and receiver. Our proposed method has the advantage of being robust to noise and interference, as it relies on analyzing the frequency-domain characteristics of the signal rather than the time-domain characteristics. In addition, it is applicable to a wide range of PRSHF systems, making it a valuable tool for distance estimation in practical applications. Overall, our approach offers a promising solution to the challenge of specifying unambiguous distance in PRSHF systems, and we believe it has significant potential for further development and refinement in future studies.

[Here] is a document full of prison statistics, most relevantly, bail rates. Bottom line: You don't have rights anymore. Each of the constitutional rights we have were set forth by Americans to protect their families from overzealous government officials. These rights are not there to protect you from your neighbors. article: Distinction among nearby poses and among symmetries of an object is challenging. In this paper, we propose a unified, group-theoretic approach to tackle both. Different from existing works which directly compare geometric features of poses or symmetries, our approach leverages the structural relationships between them as elements of Lie groups. Specifically, we represent nearby poses as elements of the Lie group SE (3) and symmetries as elements of the Lie group SO (3), and then utilize the Lie algebraic mappings between them to measure their differences. We also introduce a new metric, LieAd, that measures the geodesic distance between two Lie group elements in terms of the adjoint representation of their Lie algebra elements. By applying LieAd to nearby poses and symmetries, we can quantify their differences and similarities in a unified and consistent manner. Our experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and versatility of our approach in various contexts, including pose estimation, pose comparison, symmetry detection, and symmetry grouping.

article: The Turing Machine is the paradigmatic case of computing machines, but there are others, such as Artificial Neural Networks, Table Computing, Relational-Indeterminate Computing and diverse forms of analogical computing, each with their own strengths and limitations. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are computing systems modeled after the human brain. ANNs are capable of learning from data and adjusting their processing based on that data. They can be used for tasks such as image recognition and natural language processing. Table Computing involves using tables, which are essentially two-dimensional arrays, to represent data and perform computations. It is often used for tasks that involve large sets of data, such as database management. Relational-Indeterminate Computing is a type of computing that aims to bridge the gap between symbolic reasoning and numerical processing. It involves using algebraic and logical operations to manipulate data in a way that enables both exact and approximate computations. Analogical computing uses physical systems to perform computations. For example, an analog computer might use electrical circuits to solve equations. Analog computers are useful for tasks such as simulations and modeling. Each of these computing paradigms has its own strengths and limitations, and they are often used in combination to solve complex problems. As computing technology continues to evolve, it is likely that new paradigms will emerge, offering new possibilities for solving problems and pushing the boundaries of what is possible.

article: Why do they always show up at night? There's no hard and fast rule that ghosts only exist when it's dark out is there? I mean, would it really be such an inconvenience for them to knock on my door and make a normal fucking introduction? But noooo it's always 2 or 3 in the morning when they decide that they can finally fit you into their busy schedule of moaning and groaning. I woke up with the all too familiar feeling of being watched. My alarm clock's display traveled through a mostly empty bottle of rum, whiskey, whatever the fuck it was, and hit my bloodshot eyes as a jumbled smudge of numbers. 3:02am, or maybe it was 2:03. Who even cares at this point. I took a few deep breaths, turned on the light, and quickly turned around. Thankfully, this one decided to wait at the edge of my bed. There was one girl who thought it would be fun to lie down next to me and just stare at my bare ass until I woke up. A week later I'm trying to explain to a hooker with a black eye that I'm not a violent woman beater, I'm just scared of ghosts in my bed. Imagine how well that went over. Oh, and while I'm complaining - why can't they just wake me up? They've got no problem with barging into my home unannounced in the middle of the night, but after that they'd rather politely wait until I get up on my own and see them out of the corner of my eye. How fucking considerate. This one looked about 17 or 18 years old, dressed in all white (the girls always are for some reason). Her hair came down to the small of her back, and her eyes were wide open, with the pupils fully dilated. If you had covered the bottom half of her face you would have sworn she was screaming her lungs out. "What do you want?" I asked, probably a little too aggressively. I knew what she wanted. Everyone who came here always wanted the same thing. She didn't reply. Instead, she slowly held out her hand. Clenched in her fist was a photo of a man, slightly balding with a scraggly beard. His eyes matched the girl's and his chin had the same sharp point as hers. This was a first. Not parents killing their kids, but the kids coming back for revenge. Usually they've been raised from birth to blame themselves for whatever the twisted fucks do to them. I looked at the picture again, and then asked "Where is he?" She slowly walked to the door, and then through it. Also, can I just say, they NEVER wait for you to get your shoes on, or get your shit together, nah. They just fucking leave and you have to keep up with them or else they come back again the next night. I swear, I hate ghosts almost as much as I hate living humans. I scrambled out of bed and made a grab for my shoes - only got hold of one, but it would have to do. She was already out of my apartment. We ended up at a three story house in one of the wealthiest sections of the city. She led me right up to the driveway and then paused. They always stopped outside and waited. If they were gone by the time I came out, then I knew it had all worked out. All the lights appeared to be off inside. "Does this house have an alarm system?" I asked. She shook her head and pointed at the door. She just wanted me to walk in? I slowly grabbed the handle and turned. The door swung open swiftly and silently, no alarms going off except for the one in my head that this was a little too easy. I looked back at her, but she was rooted to the spot, waiting for me to go inside and finish the job. I crept silently through the elegantly furnished hallway, passing large paintings and expensive looking knick-knacks that looked fuck ugly but I was sure rich people were willing to spend millions on. I came to a large winding staircase, and at the very top I saw a light on in one of the rooms. Why was this so easy? Normally a hit took a few days of planning but here I was, not 30 minutes after seeing that girl and already on my way to off the target. I looked into the room and saw the back of his head. He was resting in an armchair, his head lolling slightly from side to side. I could only see the top half of his head, but I was sure it was him. The slight balding, the shape of his head, yeah this was the guy alright. Okay so normally I stage an accident, or maybe shoot from a distance, but tonight I was wearing one shoe, a ripped up tshirt and teddy bear boxers. I guess I could just snap his neck? I started to take a step closer. Suddenly the head jerked up. I froze in my tracks, trying to decide whether I should rush him and kill him now, or run back and try again with a better plan. I kept waiting for another movement but it seemed as though he had gone back to sleep. Alright, it's now or never. Just get it over with I thought. There's no point in prolonging this any more. I started to move towards him, ready to snap his neck in a quick fluid motion and then get the hell out of here. I was maybe a couple steps away when I saw the gun. Wait, what? The blast echoed all throughout the empty house. My target lay on the ground, his head a bloody unrecognizable mass. His hand still tightly wrapped around the gun, now smoking slightly. Okay, now its time to get the fuck out of here As I sprinted back out the way I came, I looked over to where I left the girl before I went inside. There was nobody there. I guess as long as the guy dies, it doesn't matter who does the job. As I made my way back up my apartment building, my heart rate started to slow down a little. That was definitely the weirdest fucking job I've ever been on. I fumbled with the keys to my apartment and finally got the right one through the lock. I collapsed onto my couch, trying to get my head around everything that happened. I didn't even need to do anything, I could have gotten my 8 hours and the guy would still be dead in the morning I rubbed my eyes and swore. There was no way I was going to be able to fall back asleep now. I turned on the TV and watched informercials for about an hour or two, until I started to feel sleepy. The sun was starting to come up, but I didn't care. I turned off the TV and made my way back to the bedroom. I woke up again to the feeling of being watched, but that was a constant these days. The alarm clock read 2:54pm, I guess it was about time to eat breakfast. I sat up, rubbing the sleep from my eyes, pushed myself off of the bed, and walked straight through her.

article: George and Julie embraced- the next twenty four hours would be the deciding factor in how their child lived and died. Now it was her and George's turn to see whether or not their persistence, research, and dedication would pay off. The trip to the hospital was uneventful. Julie flipped through Facebook posts on her phone as George drove the minivan. As usual, University Medical Center was overwhelmed with the pregnant; doctors, nurses, nervous husbands and lovers scrambling to find the right room or person to talk to. article: We consider the stochastic extensible bin packing problem (SEBP) in which n items of stochastic size are packed into m bins of unit capacity. In contrast to the classical bin packing problem, the size of each item is not fixed but follows a probability distribution. The goal is to minimize the expected number of bins used to store all items. To solve SEBP, we can use some variant of the dynamic programming (DP) algorithm. The basic idea here is to construct a sequence of tables, where each table represents the optimal solution for a subset of items. We start with the base case where we have no items, and hence, no bins are used. Then, we add items one by one and compute the optimal solution for each subset of items. At each step, we consider all possible bins that the current item can be packed into. For each bin, we compute the cost of packing the item into that bin using the best solution found so far for the remaining items. Finally, we take the minimum over all possible bins to obtain the optimal solution. The time complexity of this algorithm is O (nm2), which can be quite high for large problem instances. To reduce the running time, we can use some optimization techniques such as pruning and memoization. Moreover, we can consider some heuristics to obtain good initial solutions that can be used to prune the search space. In summary, SEBP is a challenging stochastic optimization problem that can be solved using DP or other optimization techniques. The precise approach depends on the specific problem instance and the available computational resources.

article: I recognize her the moment I appear. She has aged well. At 52, her hair is still jet black, shoulder-length and wavy in that casual, effortless look so many people strive for. Her eyes are just as sharp as they were when she was 12, green to the point of distraction, passionate and flashing. She starts a little. "You came." There is surprise in her voice. "Of course," I say. It has been 40 years of radio silence but my oath has not disappeared. I am still bound to her, whether I like it or not. She studies me like I am an interesting case and she doesn't know how to proceed. She is a lawyer now, a well-known one too. I've watched her for the past 40 years. She is the oldest person I've ever served; all the others wished almost instantly. She is the only person who has ever waited. "The rules are still the same?" she asks hesitantly. I nod. She studies me even more intently. "I see," she says at last. "Okay." I met her when she was 11, 41 years ago. She had called me by accident, she didn't know how. I didn't know how either, only that I was now bound to her. She was an excitable, confused preteen, but she was smart. The first thing she asked for was a thousand dollars to appear underneath her pillow every Monday. She could've asked for more - ten thousands or a million - but she was 11 and a thousand seemed like the world. And she'd gotten that, for the past 41 years, and she was comfortable and wealthy and never had to worry. She called me again a year later. She wanted to know whether people liked her. "Not a complicated, constant thing," I remember her saying. "Just a yesno thing. When I want to know, I want to just be able to know if someone likes me. If I ask, yes, no. That's all." And I had given it to her, and she had used it (less and less as she got older, though). She'd used it on real friends and fake friends, possible boyfriends and exes, even the man who ended up being her husband. She'd simply known if they truly liked her or not. Now I am back in her living room. I've watched her grow over the decades, mature into a successful, powerful woman. She is an exception. Usually, the ones that meet me end up going crazy. She survived. And she wants her final wish. She looks away from me. "Isn't there some sort of..... time limit on this kind of thing?" she asks hesitantly. "No," I respond. "But usually people don't wait this long." A hint of a smile appears on her face. "I didn't think so." "So what may I do for you?" I have to admit that I'm curious. I thought she'd forgotten about me. She turns back to me, her gaze piercing. "Did you know I'm 52?" she asks suddenly. "Yes," I say truthfully. "It's been 40 years." "And..... did you know I'm now considered old? Not middle-aged, old." This seems to amuse her and she smiles a bit wider. I shake my head no. "No, neither did I. I definitely don't feel old." I don't answer. She seems to forget I'm there for a moment, but then she's back. "I know my wish," she says confidently, loudly. The house is empty. Her kids are grown up and her husband is at work. "What would you like?" I ask. She is on the verge of a smirk. I can tell she's pleased with herself. She draws herself up, presents herself to me. "Genie," she announces. "I want to go back. To when I was 12, to the last time I saw you. I want to become that person again. I want to go through life again. I want to live again." I stare at her for a moment, at the rich and intelligent 52-year-old standing in front of me. She has had a good life, a lucky life. She has gotten everything she has ever wanted and she has been happy, I know she's been happy. She has had just the right amount of conflict, enough to keep her entertained. She has a job she loves, a husband she adores, kids she sees every other week. And she wants to try again, to go back. I have watched her build her life up, she has been my only success story, and she is throwing it all away. She stares back at me defiantly, daring me to refuse. We both know I can't. "Okay," I sigh at last. "Your wish is my command."

article: It smells like cigarettes. It always does in here. Nobody has smoked in here for years, but it's not an odor that time can easily erase. Something about the smel and dim lighting is soothing; refreshing, even. The only feature of the otherwise non-descript watering hole that is McNally's Irish pub, is the lack of features. Along the glossy downtown strip, it's a shadow, creeping across the face of glamour. No neon lights, no Happy Hour specials posted on the door. Just a relic from a former era when a bar was a bar. A place where relics, like myself, can come and drink to remember a time where things were simple and life was slower. No Facespace or Instatweet. Just a cold scotch and colder memories. Familiar faces with stories that are told through a series of nods and grunts. After a particularly Mondayish Thursday, I could think of no place I'd rather be than my stool at the end of the bar with 4 fingers of Powers Irish Whiskey and a pint of Budweiser. Grand dad used to call it a Polish High ball. I call it the usual. I open the door and get greeting by the sweet smell of familiarity. Tip my hat to Morgan behind the bar as I take my usual seat. By the time I've got my hat off and I'm settled in my seat, Morgan has the usual ready to do. I take a moment to remember my grand dad before I drain my whiskey. "Na zdrowie to you, Old Man." I say to myself. Unconsciouly, really. Every first round is for my Grand Dad. Before I can sit back and enjoy the quiet ramblings of Morgan's latest rounds of complaints about his neighbors (The club next to his bar is, apparently, the beginning of the end), I see her. Her. By the very gender of the word, it's cause for confusion at McNally's. Not that it's a chauvinists establishment or anything, but it generally doesn't attract ladies like a cocktail lounge or craft brewery might. Hell, Morgan only knows how to pour whisky and the two beer options are Budweiser or Not Budweiser. By the time I realize she's not an illusion, I realize something else: she's crying. Silently. Not making a fuss about it, not crying out for attention. The tears just stream down her face. She looked like the saddest person I've ever seen. Despite every inch of my body protesting, I do the unthinkable. "Uh..miss?" She turns. She's pretty. Plain, but pretty. Even crying. She just looks so damn sad. "Yes?" She has an accent. Eastern Europe? "Uh..I don't mean to bother.." Am I really that bad at this? " ....yes?" Not unpolitely, but cautious. "It's just that..... well you're there..... you just....I just want to make sure you're ok is all." Good Lord I should have kept my mouth shut. She smiles. I think. I didn't wear my glasses. "Oh. Well that's kind of you." Her accent again. Reminds me of my Grand Dad's. Polish? "I suppose I have had better days." She says. Seems private. I like that. "Haven't we all?" I offer. Well, I did my good deed for the day. This lady is ok and I'm free to pretend to be caring about Morgan's next door night club troubles (Music, loud enough to hear all the way in here after midnight. Madness). "Sir?" Shit. "Uh, yeah?" "Who did you toast to?" "What?" "Na zdrowie. It's a polish toast. I don't mean to pry, but I thought I heard you say it?" "Oh..... yea. Yea I suppose I did." I guess that accent was Polish. "Who did you toast to?" She seems geniunely curious. Oh what the hell. "My grand dad. He came from Poland. Years an' years ago. When he was a young man." "You were close with him?" "Well, yea. He taught me most things I know." She's quiet for a beat. Like she's wrestling an idea. I look to Morgan for an interuption. He's too bothered by the younger crowd peering in his windows (Don't even have the decency to dress right....). Crap. Looks like I'm on my own for this one. "He is gone now?" She asks softly. Sadly, even. "Yea. He passed some years ago." "That must have been difficult." "Well, yea." What is she getting at here? " ....I lost someone." Ah. "My condolences. That why you're crying?" "Yes." "Who did you lose?" She takes a deep breath. "My sister." "That's tough." That's when the dam broke. "Tough? Tough?! It's impossible! She wasn't sick or old! She wasn't in an accident! She just died! Dropped dead in her office at work!" She starts sobbing again. Morgan looks like he's just realizing for the first time that there's a woman in his bar. She stops crying long enough to look up and ask me a question. "How? How do I do this? How do you deal with your grand dad? Please tell me. Please. I came here to get drunk and forget. Is that it? Is that how? Is that what you do?" So that's it. She's never been hurt like this before. "No," I tell her as I hold up 2 fingers to Morgan who, desperate to be busy and away from this situation, readies 2 glasses of whisky and 2 pints of Budweiser. "That's not what I do." "Well what then?" She asks. It's desperate. She's looking for anything to help her forget. Morgan brings us 4 glasses; 2 with Powers, 2 Buds. She looks confused. She looks at the drinks as I set hers in front of her and take mine. "What was your sister's name?" " ..... Kasia." She says it almost defensively. "And your name?" "Karolina." I slide her the whiskey. Lifting my glass, I say "Na zdrowie, Kasia." and drain it. With some hesitation, so does she. She's pretty clearly new to shots and whiskey. After a few coughs and sputters, I slide her the beer. She sips it tentatively. "This is how we forget?" "No, Karolina, this is how we remember." She looks confused. I sip my beer and get comfortable. "Tell me about your sister." She hesitates, then smiles, and I know that it's going to be a long night, but it'll be worth it because she'll be ok and she'll learn how to deal with her first real life scar. Just like Grand Dad tought me.

article: Bi-Intuitionistic Stable Tense Logics (BIST Logics) are tense logics with a Kripke semantics where worlds in a frame are equipped with a pre-order as well as with an accessibility relation which is 'stable' with respect to this pre-order. BIST logics are extensions of a logic, BiSKt , which arose in the semantic context of hypergraphs, since a special case of the pre-order can represent the incidence structure of a hypergraph. In this paper we provide, for the first time, a Hilbert-style axiomatisation of BISKt and prove the strong completeness of BiSKt . We go on to prove strong completeness of a class of BIST logics obtained by extending BiSKt by formulas of a certain form. Moreover we show that the finite model property and the decidability hold for a class of BIST logics.

article: Most generative models of audio directly generate samples in one of two domains: time or frequency. While sufficient to express any signal, these representations are inefficient, as they do not capture the rich structure of audio signals. An alternative approach is to use a hybrid representation that combines both time and frequency information. One example of such a representation is the constant-Q transform, which decomposes the audio signal into multiple frequency bands with logarithmic spacing. This representation is useful because it captures both the fine structure of the audio signal in time and the harmonic structure of the sound in frequency. Additionally, it is efficient because it enables sparse processing. Another approach is to use symbolic representations of sound, such as MIDI representations or score representations. These representations are particularly useful for modeling music, where the temporal and harmonic structure is often more important than the exact sound waveform. By modeling these symbolic representations directly, generative models can generate new melodies or harmonies that sound musically plausible. Overall, the choice of representation depends on the specific application and the type of audio being modeled.

article: I stepped out, dizzy and dehydrated, shielding my eyes from blinding bright lights. My head was spinning like a carousel as I tried to find a place to sit down and re-arrange my senses. A grim looking chair, with metal cuffs on the arms, and an ungodly looking metal thing jutting out from the top had to suffice. I slumped into it, clutching my head, breathing deeply. I didn't think too much about what the device I sat in was for. I didn't really think about anything at all, to be honest. It took a minute for me to actually start looking around and start to comprehend my surroundings. White, sterile walls, quiet beeps and whirrs, strange devices strewn about the room, Pieces of paper, with frantically scrawled notes strewn about the tiled floor. I was in the centre of a genius's workspace. Removing my hand from my head, I stood up, walking around, trying to find some substantial evidence as to why I was here. Something was missing. I felt that if I saw one little bit of information, one tiny thing, I would figure out what was happening. Or, more importantly, who I was. It was by this point I realised that I was stark naked, and quickly grabbed a towel hanging off a table on the right side of the room to save my embarrassment. After I wrapped the towel around my waist, I paused for thought. ' Why would I be embarrassed? There's no one here.' But, certainly, there was someone here earlier. A cup of coffee, still steaming, sat on the table. A Computer on the opposite side of the room was switched on, prominently displaying a document containing a wall of text. I decided to investigate further. Sitting at the computer, I scrolled through the text, which seemed like a sort of speech that one would present to an audience, and, through the eloquent wordings and descriptions, I figured out two things. One, this room belonged to a scientist. Two, they were on the verge of a breakthrough. This breakthrough in particular interested me, partly due to my curiosity, but mostly due to the way they described it as " The most astonishing breakthrough in scientific history. " Suffice it to say, I wanted to know what was at work in this den of science. Before I walked back to the table, to take a look at some of the documents, I looked back to where I entered the room, and proceeded to kick myself for not looking before. A giant, steel, behemoth of a machine met my eyes. Two pods, each with a door, were connected to a huge box of blinking buttons and flashing lights. One pod, presumably mine, was already open, with the dark, chrome interior being fully illuminated. The other pod was still closed. After taking my good look at the machine, I turned to the table, picking up a note with copious amounts of equations, underlinings and encircled passages scattered across the page. Not one thing pointed to what the ' breakthrough'might be. Page after page, only numbers and calculations met my eyes. I was on the verge of giving up, until I noticed a whiteboard next to the computer. Two big words made everything very clear. " Cloning Experiments. " And there it was. There was the answer I was looking for. I, or should I say, they, had managed to clone themselves, and I was the result. Scientific breakthrough indeed! I looked back at the great machine. The second pod was still closed. Jogging towards it, I smiled, gripping the handle, and pulling open the door, readying myself to greet whomever was inside. Dead, empty sockets. Grey, peeling skin. Thin, loose hair. I was dead. I'd failed miserably.

article: My old bones creaked as long disused muscles hauled me up the cold mountain road. It's been sixteen years since the floodwaters released my coffin from my grave, since my eyes burned at the first light in countless decades. My mind had long since lost language and misplaced memories. The dark will do that to you. The first few days, or months maybe, I had passed the time remembering the songs from my village tavern, the stories from my family's past, and the lovely girls who no doubt awaited my return. I expected my family to release me any moment, as soon as the cemetery sexton could be bought off. Days turned to months, and I felt the ground grow cold around me. I don't remember giving up. I didn't care at first, I knew I could pop up in another village a few hundred miles away, build a life, and forget the circumstance of my unfortunate disposition. As my waiting grew longer I grew more angry at the bastards who put me in that hole. They knew what they did to me. I don't remember going mad. But surely I did. And then nothing. Nothing until I felt my coffin sliding, and breaking up, and water filling my mouth and nose and lungs. I washed up on the shore, no idea who or where or why I was. Months later and with the kindness of strangers, I started to think again. In time, slowly, my memories returned, in little snippets at first. Confusion as my new language clashed with the tongue of my memories. And then, hatred. Anger. A desire for revenge. It took me four years to piece together enough memories to fully understand what happened to me. I was a John Smith, an unknown, a medical marvel with amnesia. article: Insider trading, for those of you who aren't familiar with the term, is the practice of trading (i.e. buying or selling) a public company's stock by individuals with non-public knowledge about the company. Inside trading is considered a felony. For example, in 2001 Martha Stewart had a significant amount of stock in a drug company called ImClone. When a new drug by ImClone failed to get FDA approval, Stewart's broker tipped her off that the stock prices were about to fall dramatically. Stewart sold 230,000 in ImClone shares the day before the failure to get FDA approval became public knowledge. Ultimately, Stewart was found guilty of insider trading, which lead to five months in prison, five months of home confinement, and two years probation. Stewart is now a convicted felon. This all brings me to my point of this CMV. I can think of no reason why insider trading should be considered illegal, and especially why it should be considered a felony. Typically the designation of felony is reserved for only the most heinous of crimes- such as murder, rape, assault, etc. It is absurd to believe that insider trading is anywhere near these crimes. Some may say that insider trading should be illegal as it gives some people an unfair advantage when it comes to buying and selling stocks. But is that really a good enough reasoning to make it illegal? There are numerous legal ways that people can gain an unfair advantage in the stock world- certainly nobody is going to arrest Warren Buffett's daughter if Buffett gives her stock advice. Furthermore, who exactly gets harmed by insider trading? Insider trading may be the ultimate example of a victimless crime. Insider trading results when a willing buyer and a willing seller agree to trade property that the seller rightfully owns, with no prior contract being made between the parties to refrain from trading if there is asymmetric information. Even Milton Friedman, a Nobel laureate in economics said- "You want more insider trading, not less. You want to give the people most likely to have knowledge about deficiencies of the company an incentive to make the public aware of that." So there you go, CMV. Try and change my view on insider trading. EDIT: Wow, I'm really REALLY overwhelmed by the amount of responses this post has gotten. I'm pretty sure my view has been changed, but I can't really point out a single post that changed my view, so I'm not sure what to do about deltas. If you really want a delta and think you deserved one, message me and I'll read through your post. If it helped change my view, I'll give you the delta. Thanks for the discussion, CMV. I will fully admit that I didn't know much about economics coming into this thread, and that I was fully aware that my view on insider trading was lacking and came from a place of ignorance. I'm glad that I got a chance to learn a lot on the subject, as there are obviously many people here that know infinitely more about economics than I do. Once again, thank you.

article: A sparsifier of a graph G (Benczur and Karger; Spielman and Teng) is a sparse weighted subgraph G that approximately retains the same cut structure of G . For general graphs, non-trivial sparsification is possible only by using weighted graphs in which different edges have different weights. Even for graphs that admit unweighted sparsifiers (that is, sparsifiers in which all the edge weights are equal to the same scaling factor), there are no known polynomial time algorithms that find such unweighted sparsifiers. We study a weaker notion of sparsification suggested by Oveis Gharan, in which the number of cut edges in each cut (S , S) is not approximated within a multiplicative factor ( 1 ), but is, instead, approximated up to an additive term bounded by times d S vol (S), where d is the average degree of the graph and vol (S) is the sum of the degrees of the vertices in S . We provide a probabilistic polynomial time construction of such sparsifiers for every graph, and our sparsifiers have a near-optimal number of edges O ( - 2 n polylog ( 1 . We also provide a deterministic polynomial time construction that constructs sparsifiers with a weaker property having the optimal number of edges O ( - 2 n). Our constructions also satisfy a spectral version of the "additive sparsification" property. Notions of sparsification have also been studied for hypergraphs. Our construction of "additive sparsifiers" with O (n) edges also works for hypergraphs, and provides the first non-trivial notion of sparsification for hypergraphs achievable with O (n) hyperedges when and the rank r of the hyperedges are constant. Finally, we provide a new construction of spectral hypergraph sparsifiers, according to the standard definition, with poly ( - 1 , r) n log n hyperedges, improving over the previous spectral construction (Soma and Yoshida) that used O (n 3) hyperedges even for constant r and .

article: Multi-target multi-camera tracking (MTMCT) systems track targets across cameras. Due to the continuity of target trajectories, tracking systems usually restrict their data association within a local neighborhood. In single camera tracking, data association is typically based on the appearance or motion model of the targets. However, MTMCT systems face additional challenges, such as occlusion and camera view changes, which can cause significant shifts in appearance and motion. To overcome these challenges, researchers have developed various techniques for MTMCT, including tracklet-based association, graph-based association, and deep learning-based methods. Tracklet-based association uses short-term trajectory segments, called tracklets, to associate targets across cameras. Graph-based association constructs a global graph, where nodes represent targets and edges represent spatial and temporal relationships between them. Deep learning-based methods use neural networks to learn features that are robust to appearance changes and occlusions, which can improve data association performance. Overall, the development of MTMCT systems is an active research area and continues to advance with the aid of new technologies and improved algorithms.

article: We introduce neural networks for end-to-end differentiable proving of queries to knowledge bases by operating on dense vector representations of symbols. These neural networks are constructed recursively by taking inspiration from the backward chaining algorithm as used in Prolog. Specifically, we replace symbolic unification with a differentiable computation on vector representations of symbols using a radial basis function kernel, thereby combining symbolic reasoning with learning subsymbolic vector representations. By using gradient descent, the resulting neural network can be trained to infer facts from a given incomplete knowledge base. It learns to (i) place representations of similar symbols in close proximity in a vector space, (ii) make use of such similarities to prove queries, (iii) induce logical rules, and (iv) use provided and induced logical rules for multi-hop reasoning. We demonstrate that this architecture outperforms ComplEx, a state-of-the-art neural link prediction model, on three out of four benchmark knowledge bases while at the same time inducing interpretable function-free first-order logic rules.

article: The adoption of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) in wireless networks can enhance the spectrum- and energy-efficiency by controlling the propagation environment. Although the RIS does not consume any transmit power, the circuit power of the RIS cannot be ignored, especially when the number of reflecting elements is large. In this paper, we propose the joint design of beamforming vectors at the base station, active RIS set, and phase-shift matrices at the active RISs to minimize the network power consumption, including the RIS circuit power consumption, while taking into account each user's target data rate requirement and each reflecting element's constant modulus constraint. However, the formulated problem is a mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) problem, which is NP-hard. To this end, we present an alternating optimization method, which alternately solves second order cone programming (SOCP) and MIQP problems to update the optimization variables. Specifically, the MIQP problem is further transformed into a semidefinite programming problem by applying binary relaxation and semidefinite relaxation. Finally, an efficient algorithm is developed to solve the problem. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the network power consumption and reveal the importance of taking into account the RIS circuit power consumption.

article: This article presents the method of steganography detection, which is formedby replacing the least significant bit (LSB). Detection is performed bydividing the image into layers and making an analysis of the LSBs in each layer. The goal of steganography detection is to determine if an image has been modified to hide information. The LSB replacement method involves changing the LSB of each pixel in an image to encode information. This method is often used by steganography techniques to hide messages or other data within an image. To detect steganography using LSB replacement, the image is divided into layers, and the LSBs of each layer are analyzed. The analysis involves looking for patterns or inconsistencies in the LSBs that suggest the presence of hidden information. One technique used to detect steganography is to compare the distribution of LSBs in the image to that of an unmodified image. If the distribution of the LSBs in the image being analyzed is significantly different from the unmodified image, it may be an indication of steganography. Another technique is to examine the LSBs of neighboring pixels to identify any patterns or changes that suggest the presence of hidden data. For example, if the LSBs in a certain area of the image appear to be abnormally consistent, it may be an indication that they have been modified to hide information. In conclusion, steganography detection is an important technique for identifying images that have been modified to hide data. The LSB replacement method is a common steganography technique that can be detected by analyzing the LSBs in each layer of the image. By detecting steganography, it is possible to identify potentially harmful or illegal activities and prevent misuse of digital media.

Part tropical paradise, part unforgiving desert, the homeland of the Dwarves is believed by many to be the birthplace of civilization as we know it. Those that inhabit the empire are called Sun Dwarves, distinct from Cold Dwarves, the product of an exodus that that split the empire some time in the ancient past. There, they build their massive monuments to their revered ancestors and sun deities, and practice a strange kind of necromancy that preserves their deceased emperors to watch over their lands even in death. Further north, we find realms inhabited by a mix of Cold Dwarves, Orcs and Ogres (See Orcs). Further still we find the unforgiving wastes of Kastrunn, inhabited only be snow beasts and bloodthirsty tribes of Jerren. Orcs are a race of sturdy, colorful creatures seemingly built to weather adversity. Standing on average nearly six and a half feet tall, they are not actually a naturally-occuring creature. In some ancient age of terror, they were created by some black magic to serve as peerless soldiers of darkness. Though freed from that yoke, their bred dedication to order and hierarchy persists. Industrious and organized, Orcish kingdoms tend to be militaristic affairs, and most orc kings are also greatest tactician in their land. Orcish military doctrine frowns on pre-emptive strikes, instead emphasizing extreme retributive action - "Crush your enemies hard enough that your children don't have to," as one famous tactician once said. Several Orc nations exist to the north of the Solar Empire, as well as in the lowlands of Seceth and the mountains of Flikx. Ogres, once thought to be a separate species from Orcs, instead seem to be grown from the same stock as the original orcs. Though they can interbreed, the idea is frowned on among most of both groups. They are welcome in the orcs' kingdoms and armies, however. When found in the wild, they tend to live in nomadic clans and tribes that shy away from contact with outsiders. Jerren are short, stocky creatures with pink skin, hairy feet and immense appetites. The thought of their warbands brings a chill to even the hardiest orcish commander. Known for their immense appetites, both for food, specifically meat, even more specifically still-living meat, and sexual perversion, they bring terror wherever they roam, turning on each other if they go too long without a raid. Little is known of their internal culture, for they are universally hostile towards other creatures. Elves are a curiosity among creatures of this world, in part because they are not truly of this world. Considered the youngest of the races of the world, the first elves were creatures of flesh created by entities of the writhing chaos outside of our world. Designed by these entities to be tall, fair, powerful, and universally alluring, their sorcerers and armies nearly brought about the ruin of the world. After their seeming extinction at the end of the last war, pockets came out of wherever they had been hiding and begged the other races for forgiveness, claiming to have broken their otherworldly masters' chains. Today, there is one elven city, a city in the clouds, built on the remains of the Eldritch Portal they originally came through. How could I have waited this long to come to him? If I had come sooner would he have been awake sooner? All my fear and anger at myself vanished when he smiled at me. He didn't blame me? We talked the whole next day and I came day after day when I was done with work. He had to stay in the hospital a few more weeks and after that had to undergo physical therapy to walk again. The voice gradually changed to a happy and mildly broken tone. Then evened out to be pure joy; although still toneless I found it beautiful. I don't know why it was different on that day, but sometimes I wish the voice had urged me forward sooner. I'm not sure why I ran past the desk and to his room or why I touched Thomas. article: Imitation learning has traditionally been applied to learn a single task from demonstrations thereof. However, recent developments in imitation learning such as behavior cloning and inverse reinforcement learning have enabled broader and more diverse use cases. Behavior cloning involves simply copying the actions from demonstration data to learn a policy. This approach can be effective for simple tasks with clear demonstrations, but it can also result in a lack of flexibility in handling novel situations. In contrast, inverse reinforcement learning involves trying to deduce the underlying reward function of the demonstrator given their behavior. This approach can lead to more generalizable policies that can handle novel situations. Furthermore, developments in multi-task and meta learning have allowed imitation learning to be applied more effectively to tasks with complex and diverse sets of skills. These approaches allow the agent to learn to learn, or to learn to transfer skills learned from one task to another. article: Given only data generated by a standard confounding graph with unobserved confounder, the Average Treatment Effect (ATE) is not identifiable. Controlling for the confounding variable involves including it as a covariate in the statistical analysis model. This assumes that all relevant confounders have been measured and included in the model. Instrumental variables are external variables that are correlated with the treatment but not directly correlated with the outcome. This method is used when there is a random assignment of treatment. Propensity score matching involves creating a model that predicts the probability of receiving treatment based on observed variables. In this method, treated and untreated individuals are matched based on their propensity scores to create a more balanced sample, and the ATE is estimated based on this matched sample.

article: The classical perceptron is a simple neural network that performs a binary classification by a linear mapping between static inputs and outputs and application of a threshold. For small inputs, neural networks in a stationary state also perform an effectively linear input-output transformation, but of an entire time series. Choosing the temporal mean of the time series as the feature for classification, the linear transformation of the network with subsequent thresholding is equivalent to the classical perceptron. Here we show that choosing covariances of time series as the feature for classification maps the neural network to what we call a 'covariance perceptron'; a mapping between covariances that is bilinear in terms of weights. By extending Gardner's theory of connections to this bilinear problem, using a replica symmetric mean-field theory, we compute the pattern and information capacities of the covariance perceptron in the infinite-size limit. Closed-form expressions reveal superior pattern capacity in the binary classification task compared to the classical perceptron in the case of a high-dimensional input and low-dimensional output. For less convergent networks, the mean perceptron classifies a larger number of stimuli. However, since covariances span a much larger input and output space than means, the amount of stored information in the covariance perceptron exceeds the classical counterpart. For strongly convergent connectivity it is superior by a factor equal to the number of input neurons. Theoretical calculations are validated numerically for finite size systems using a gradient-based optimization of a soft-margin, as well as numerical solvers for the NP hard quadratically constrained quadratic programming problem, to which training can be mapped.

article: We give a (2) -approximation algorithm for minimizing total weighted completion time on a single machine under release time and precedence constraints. This settles a recent conjecture made in the scheduling community regarding the existence of such an algorithm. To give some background, the problem of minimizing total weighted completion time on a single machine is a classic problem in scheduling theory. It involves scheduling a set of n jobs, each with a processing time pi and a weight wi, on a single machine. The goal is to minimize the sum of weighted completion times of the jobs, subject to the constraint that each job cannot start processing before a certain release time ri, and that some jobs have precedence constraints (i.e., one job must finish before another can start). The recent conjecture in the scheduling community was whether there exists a (2) -approximation algorithm for this problem when there are release time and precedence constraints. The (2) -approximation algorithm we present confirms this conjecture. The algorithm works by first sorting the jobs in non-decreasing order of their release times. Then, we schedule the jobs in this order, using a modified earliest-start-time rule. Under this rule, we compute, for each job i, the earliest start time si such that all jobs with a precedence constraint on i have finished processing by si. We then assign job i to start processing at time si. It can be shown that this algorithm produces a feasible schedule, since it respects all release time and precedence constraints. Furthermore, the algorithm has a 2-approximation ratio, meaning that the total weighted completion time of the schedule produced by the algorithm is at most twice the optimal solution. Overall, this algorithm provides a practical and efficient solution for the problem of minimizing total weighted completion time on a single machine with release time and precedence constraints.

article: Crossposted from a comment on rskeptic I've read David Fitzgerald, some of Richard Carrier, and the criticisms of both and it seems to me that there is a lot of vitriol on both sides. The mythicists take umbrage at being dismissed as amateurs and dabblers and vociferously defend their hypotheses, the historicists take umbrage at the strenuous attacks, and it all gets very torrid very quickly, and becomes very difficult to actually analyze the actual strength of the arguments. So, as a skeptic, I'm sufficiently intrigued by the Mythicist arguments to profess agnosticism as to the Historical Jesus, for the following reasons: There are no extrabiblical attestations of any significant event from the life of Jesus. On the contrary, events such as the slaughter of the innocents, the census of all the Empire are clearly fictitious, and multiple miracles, the triumphal entry to Jerusalem, and multiple events surrounding the crucifixion are absent from all historical records when there's a reasonable chance that some account of them would have survived, had they occurred at all. The synoptic problem indicates that we are working from at most one source that even approaches being primary, and even that most likely written much later, anonymously, and as hagiography rather than history. Well into the third century, pagan sources mostly recount the existence of Christians and document the claims of Christians. This is at best hearsay. attempts to reconstruct the "real" historical Jesus are invariably unprovable and contradictory with one anotherthere is no consensus. While the vast bulk of NT scholarship presumes an historical Jesus, the "scholarly consensus" should be given less weight since for centuries, such research has been largely a devotional undertaking. Jesus mythicism is very nearly literally heretical, as well as figuratively. At least sufficiently that it deserves consideration even though a strong consensus exists that contradicts it. So, we accept the historical reality of many persons throughout ancient history based on much less proof than gospels and various other pagan mentions. So maybe there was an itinerant sage named Yeshua who ran around, gathered a minor following, and was executed for sedition. But the problems above mean A) we know nothing about him and B) almost everything written about him is unknowable or outright fictitious. I look at it as the difference between "Abraham Lincoln" and "Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter." Notwithstanding that there is an historical person that was the basis, the hero version is a myth. The most popular approach is probably the Bron-Kerbosch algorithm, which is an efficient way to find all cliques in a graph. article: In this paper, we study a new representation-learning task, which we termed as disassembling object representations. Given an image featuring multiple objects, the goal of disassembling is to acquire a latent representation, of which each part corresponds to one category of objects. Disassembling thus finds its application in a wide domain such as image editing and few- or zero-shot learning, as it enables category-specific modularity in the learned representations. To this end, we propose an unsupervised approach to achieving disassembling, named Unsupervised Disassembling Object Representation (UDOR). UDOR follows a double auto-encoder architecture, in which a fuzzy classification and an object-removing operation are imposed. The fuzzy classification constrains each part of the latent representation to encode features of up to one object category, while the object-removing, combined with a generative adversarial network, enforces the modularity of the representations and integrity of the reconstructed image. Furthermore, we devise two metrics to respectively measure the modularity of disassembled representations and the visual integrity of reconstructed images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed UDOR, despited unsupervised, achieves truly encouraging results on par with those of supervised methods.

article: Just today, I saw mention of a story that some lawyer named Larry Klayman is attempting to have President Barack Obama deported due to his perceived lack of citizenship. This hearkens back to the "birther" movement, and all of the conservatives who have some mistaken conception that our president wasn't actually born in Hawaii, and therefore is not a US citizen, and is therefore not eligible to hold office. Aside from that, however, it got me to wondering - what would it matter if that were true? What if Obama were born in Kenya, then moved to the United States at a very young age, was raised here, and lived his life working towards becoming a public servant and eventually president? Is there any indication that he's not fulfilled his obligations in the exact same way as someone who was physically born in the US, instead of some East African nation? Which brought me back to something I've thought about before: Why do we still cling to Article II, Section 1, Clause 5 of the US Constitution, which stipulates that the president must be a natural-born citizen of the United States? I understand its importance in a historical context - as a fledgling nation, we needed to be assured of the patriotism of any potential Chief Executive. But in the 21st century, the United States is a much more variegated population, and we've already seen some prominent politicians who wouldn't qualify to serve as president based on that strict standard, such as Arnold Schwarzenegger, or one of my favorites, former Michigan governor Jennifer Granholm. So, I believe it's time to revisit this section of the Constitution, and amend it to include naturalized citizens. We can leave in the part that requires a 14 year residence, or even increase it, if we're that concerned, but I think following a dedicated leader who has lived in this country long enough to be interested in serving it in a fairly thankless job is proof enough that they wouldn't abuse the position to unduly serve their birth nation instead. article: We present a random access method inspired on Bloom filters that is suited for Machine-Type Communications (MTC). Each accessing device sends a signature during the contention process. A signature is a bit string that represents the information that the device wants to transmit. This signature is then hashed and multiple indices in the Bloom filter are updated. The Bloom filter is used to determine which indices are already set, and a device can avoid a collision by selecting an index that is not already set. Once the device has successfully selected an index, it transmits its data using that index. The receiver of the data can then determine the corresponding signature by searching the Bloom filter for the index. This random access method has several advantages for MTC applications. First, it is highly scalable, as the Bloom filter can easily accommodate a very large number of signatures. Second, it is highly efficient, as the Bloom filter can quickly check which indices are already set, allowing devices to avoid collisions. Overall, this random access method has the potential to greatly improve the performance of MTC networks by minimizing collisions and increasing throughput.
